correctness.rationale: The model fixes Poisson redraw rate alpha (not sign-flip rate), and independent Brownian coefficient D. Inverting the 2x2 tilted generator gives G=(s+alpha)/(s(s+alpha)+v^2 q^2) with s=Dq^2-iomega. Direct complex division produces the displayed strictly-positive-denominator response sign. The weak-potential force follows from a separately derived stationary density balance, including the Fourier sign. AM-GM gives the necessary no-positive-power region and the strict converse is realized by explicitly nonnegative Schwartz wave packets. Plancherel and two-sided Fourier concentration justify the sharp L2 variational supremum. At D=Dc(1-eta), the entire negative spectral support concentrates at (q,V)=(2alpha/v,0); its uniform two-scale expansion and disk maximization yield exactly 4alpha^2/(9v^2)*eta^2. The standalone independent-matrix numerical tests, quadrature and optimization confirm finite calculations, not infinite conclusions.

value.rationale: Thermal diffusion is an experimentally natural stabilizing control in active microrheology. The exact universal cutoff answers whether any weak, localized nonnegative probe can harvest positive mechanical power at a specified speed, while the inverse statement excludes the effect for every localized probe above threshold. Near the boundary, the new L2-normalized best-possible power measures physically meaningful achievable response per interaction budget and has a nontrivial quadratic vanishing coefficient; the speed and wave-number selection explain its mechanism. The object and normalization are fixed by the force quadratic form, not chosen as an arbitrary slice. The result is restricted to weak-coupling ideal baths and does not overstate device performance.
